No repository setting changed: only `ci-pass` is required and the verdict is derived from its `needs` map, so the new lane is gated by the context that already exists. `TC-0017-0043`'s pinned set gains the name, which is how the addition arrives as a failing equality rather than as a diff nobody reads. - The new job carries no condition and appears in no `dependencyConditions` entry, which `retired BR` requires of a lane moved into a job of its own. `TC-0017-0012` asserts it by resolving each exempt lane to its host job — through a step that names the lane, or through the aggregate whose script does. - The hygiene lane does not enforce that pair. Measured: with a detection-derived condition on the new job and the job added to `dependencyConditions`, `node scripts/check-workflow-hygiene.mjs --root .` exits 0. `TDD-0094` is the seeded row for the lane-level rule and stays `todo`; enforcing it there needs the exempt-lane list declared where the lane can read it, which is a decision of its own. - Related: AC-0017-0014, retired BR, retired BR, retired BR, NFR-0001, NFR-0002, NFR-0004, `DR-0017-0011`, `DR-0017-0012`, `DR-0017-0013`, `DR-0017-0015`, `DR-0017-0016` | DONE |
| DEC-0344 | .qfai/spec/spec-0017/07_Decisions.md#DR-0017-0018: the code path leaves NFR-0002, and what it costs is pinned instead | - Status: accepted - Context: `NFR-0002` capped a code-path pull request at 12 job instances / 8 frozen-lockfile installs / 3-or-5 bundler builds, against a baseline of 14 / 13 / 6. Measured from the tree, a code path runs **26 instances / 24 installs / 5 build executions**, declaring **350 minutes** of ceiling. Nothing regressed: the `test` and `node-floor` matrices were each widened to nine legs to shorten the wall clock, and each widening was recorded. What was never re-priced is the requirement's own figure, and `.qfai/evidence/sdd-spec-0017.md` had already noted the gap and left it alone because correcting it read as a cost claim. - Decision, the unit: the code-path figures stay in instances, installs and builds. `DR-0017-0015` settled that for this requirement — converting one part of it to minutes would leave one requirement carrying two units — and this record does not reopen it. The minutes figure the pin also carries lives in the declaration beside them, never in `NFR-0002`, which is exactly where the documentation-only half already keeps its own minutes sum. - Decision, the shape: a pin with a re-pin obligation, not a ceiling. Enforcement is equality against a value recomputed from the same tree, so a clause forbidding a higher cost could not fail; what the pin refuses is a change that moved the cost and did not move the figure. `scripts/pin-code-path-cost.mjs` writes it and the hygiene lane's `code-path-cost-pin` rule reads it, both importing one computation. - Decision, the requirement: the code path **leaves `NFR-0002`**, whose subject is consumption falling. On a code path it did not fall. It rose, on purpose, and the reason is the requirement next door: nine legs finishing together cost fewer runner minutes than one leg running them in series, and count more instances — so an instance figure on a code path moves against the very thing `NFR-0002` is named for, while the wall clock it buys is `NFR-0001`'s subject. A requirement that claimed a fall here would be false on the tree that satisfies the design. `NFR-0002` keeps the documentation-only claim, where consumption does fall and the figure is five executed instances. - Decision, what is NOT claimed: that the figures are acceptable. This record prices the code path; it does not argue the price. `retired BR` governs a cost claim, and none is made here. - Decision, three limits of the measure, named rather than smoothed over: - **`buildJobs` counts jobs, not executions.** Two of the three condition their build step on `matrix.slice == 'e2e' \|\| matrix.slice == 'integration'`, so an execution count needs a GitHub expression evaluated and the lane evaluates none. The five executions are real and no lane counts them. The jobs figure still moves when a build is added to or removed from a job. - **The pin is not compared with a run.** Reading what a run actually cost needs the forge's API and a finished run, which no lint lane has. A tree that was always more expensive than it declared is therefore outside the rule, and that gap is deliberate: it is the one `.qfai/specs/spec-0017/10_Plan.md` leaves to the wall-clock reading of a pull request. - **`timeout-minutes` is a declared worst case.** The 350-minute sum sits far above what the path costs — two green runs measured 38.0 and 39.0 runner-minutes. It still catches a runaway job and a forgotten raise, which is the class a declared ceiling can catch. - Consequences: - `NFR-0002`'s code-path ceiling is gone, and every artifact that read it is corrected in the same change. Nothing in the tree asserted those numbers, so no test changes because of the removal — which is itself the finding: the code-path half had no falsifiable artifact behind it, and the figure went stale in silence. - Two readers compute the figures independently: the hygiene lane through its own collector, and the topology test through its own parse of `ci.yml`. Equality between two readings of one tree is what a single implementation cannot give itself. - A slice added to either matrix, a ceiling raised, an install introduced or a build moved between jobs now fails until the pinner has run. - Related: retired BR, NFR-0001, NFR-0002, OC-80, `DR-0017-0012`, `DR-0017-0015`, `DR-0017-0017` | DONE |
| DEC-0345 | .qfai/spec/spec-0017/07_Decisions.md#DR-0017-0019: release uploads require a complete successful gate path | - Status: accepted - Context: release prerequisites have two valid result maps. The sliced path runs `gate-tests` and `gate-floor`; the whole path runs `gate-floor-whole`. Both require `verify` and `gate`. Excluding failure and cancellation alone also accepts a required gate that was skipped or supplied no result. - Decision: each upload condition accepts only the successful selected path and skipped inactive gates. An unknown shape refuses upload. GitHub Release remains push-only, and npm publication retains manual dispatch. Environment approval, permissions, tag identity and packed-artifact verification are unchanged. - Scope: this is the release publication barrier. The change-detected `ci-pass` verdict still permits its declared skips. The shipped templates have no release or registry publication jobs. - Sequencing: harden this barrier before adding release gate jobs. Operation extraction must extend tag capability detection and these result-map tests. - Baseline: [successful release run 35414209463](https://github.com/aganesy/QFAI/actions/runs/35414209463), source `4fc271880d30ea7ab66f6584dbdfee722f3afb7f`, on 2026-09-19. The jobs API reports `gate` at 137 seconds, its checks step at 112 seconds, and its post-build leakage scan at 4 seconds. The remaining 21 seconds cover setup, cleanup and step boundaries. Against the declared 30-minute timeout, headroom is 1,663 seconds (92.4 percent). - The gate log places the lint lane starts near 01:58:01 UTC and the type check start at 01:59:02 UTC. Type checking and the first build together end near 01:59:29 UTC; pack verification ends near 01:59:52 UTC. These are approximate log intervals, not separate operation timers: the first build wrapper buffers its output until completion, so type checking cannot be separated from that build using line timestamps. - The last gate to finish is `gate-tests (pr-fix)`, at 02:03:42 UTC after 261 seconds on its runner. `verify` started at 01:57:27 UTC, so the gate phase spans 375 seconds including scheduling. All job durations sum to 2,118 seconds (35.3 runner-minutes). Publication starts at 03:57:42 UTC behind approval; that wait must not be credited to gate execution. This is one baseline run, not a before/after comparison or evidence of a performance improvement. - Remaining independent blocks: SSOT sync plus its diff; the four lint lanes; type checking; and the build, pack and post-build scan chain. Extraction needs isolated checkouts and tag-declared entry points. Checkout precedes the sidecar, setup precedes its consumers, and artifact generation precedes artifact scans. - Related: AC-0017-0035, retired BR, TC-0017-0088, TC-0017-0089 | DONE |
| DEC-0346 | .qfai/spec/spec-0017/07_Decisions.md#DR-0017-0020: release checks use isolated jobs when the tag declares their entry points | - Status: accepted - Decision: `verify` publishes both suite and checks capabilities from the tagged manifests. The checks capability is `operations` only when the suite is sliced and all four operation scripts are declared. Every other runnable tag uses `aggregate`. The manifests are data; their command bodies are never evaluated by the classifier. - The three valid paths are sliced/operations, sliced/aggregate and whole/aggregate. Publication requires successful selected jobs and skipped inactive jobs. An unknown output or whole/operations refuses publication. - Each operation job checks out the verified tag before fetching the shared setup action at the workflow revision. The sidecar keeps `clean: false`. No new job has write permissions or publication credentials. Lint skips the branch-name version pin because `verify` already checked the tag version. - Local `ci:gate:checks` calls the four entry points serially, in its original order. The workflow changes scheduling, not the set or order of commands inside each operation. The suite runs exactly once per runtime on every valid path. \| Operation \| Inputs and effects \| Dependency retained \| \| ------------------------------------ \| ----------------------------------------------------------------------- \| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ \| \| Verify tag and classify capabilities \| Tag ref and manifests; publishes immutable SHA, version and both shapes \| All consumers wait for this trust decision \| \| SSOT sync and tracked-tree diff \| Tag tree; sync may rewrite tracked assistant files \| The diff must read the synchronized tree \| \| Lint \| Tag tree; existing four lanes start together \| Setup precedes each lane; existing lane command ordering is preserved \| \| Types \| Tag source and declarations; tsc writes dist and incremental state \| Compiler verification precedes compilation; source compilation precedes test type checking \| \| Build, pack and leakage scan \| Tag source and assets; bundler and pack both rebuild dist \| The two writers stay serial, and leakage scanning reads the final build \| \| Sliced package suites \| Tag source; integration and e2e also read a local build \| Each relevant slice builds before its tests, on both runtime ranges \| \| Whole-tag fallback \| The old tag's complete aggregate and floor suite \| Its scripts define the checks that tag supports; operation scripts cannot be assumed \| \| GitHub Release and npm publication \| Successful selected gates, verified tag and inspected package \| All selected gates precede upload; approval precedes npm publication \| - Isolation is required: tsc writes `dist/` while the bundler cleans it. Running both in one checkout would race. SSOT also writes files that lint reads; separate checkouts let lint inspect the committed source while the sync job independently refuses any drift. No generated output passes between the operation jobs. - Cost declaration for a tag-push sliced path, counting publication after approval: 22 executed job instances become 25; declared timeout minutes sum from 520 to 545. The added jobs each install their own dependencies. These are topology counts, not runner-minute measurements or cost ceilings. Whole and older sliced paths retain their previous executing jobs; the added jobs are skipped. - Measurement boundary: the baseline is `DR-0017-0019`. The roughly 61-second lint interval is independent of types and build/pack work, but the baseline does not isolate every operation's duration. The topology and execution fixtures prove eligibility, complete coverage, isolation and refusal paths; they do not measure hosted runner scheduling. A comparable completed release run is still needed for actual overlap, per-operation duration, setup overhead, deadline headroom, total runner-minutes and a before/after wall-clock claim. No release is created or published to obtain that measurement. - Scope: these jobs build this repository's package. The shipped workflow templates have no corresponding release checks. - Related: AC-0017-0036, retired BR, TC-0017-0090, TC-0017-0091, TC-0017-0092 | DONE |
| DEC-0347 | .qfai/spec/spec-0017/07_Decisions.md#DR-0017-0021: exempt lint hosts remain unconditional in the hygiene declaration | - Status: accepted - Decision: `unconditionalDependencies` names the jobs hosting the exempt lint lanes. A missing, empty, malformed or duplicate list is invalid. - The independent topology assertion resolves every exempt command to its host and compares those hosts with the declaration. The hygiene lane can therefore reject a matching workflow condition and skip declaration even on a path that does not run the topology tests. - The declaration owns job names; the rule does not hard-code today's hosts. Removing a host from this declaration is a reviewed exemption change, and the topology equality still refuses it while the host runs an exempt command. - The declaration plus independent host equality enforces the existing exemption without a second workflow parser or changed allowed skip conditions. - Related: retired BR, TC-0017-0012, TC-0017-0085 | DONE |

| DEC-0379 | .qfai/spec/spec-0018/07_Decisions.md#DR-0018-0002: step 1 moves entry by entry and moves a colliding entry aside | - Status: accepted - Context: once the assistant tree is renamed, `qfai init` writes `skill/` and `agent/` before a project can migrate, so step 1 always finds some destinations already present. The skill does not require a clean working tree, so a legacy directory may hold an adopter's uncommitted edits. - Decision: move each legacy directory entry by entry. An entry whose destination is absent is renamed into it, so an adopter's own skill lands in `skill/`. An entry whose destination exists is moved to `.qfai/evidence/migration-spec-to-story/legacy/<dir>/` and listed under `## Operations`. The emptied legacy directory is then removed. Nothing is deleted, no report section is added, and the write set is unchanged. - Decision, rejected alternatives: deleting the legacy governed directories, which can lose uncommitted edits (the author's recommendation, which the author flagged as critical); listing each conflict for a person, which adds a `## For a person` section step 1 does not print; refusing with exit 2, which would fire on every project. - Consequences: a second run finds nothing to move and changes nothing. A file holding content with no destination goes to `.qfai/evidence/migration-spec-to-story/retired/<spec-id>/` instead of being deleted, so the evidence pointers of the old ledgers still resolve. A directory left empty is removed. - Decision, rejected alternatives: deleting files with no destination (the author's recommendation); a final sweep step; leaving removal to a person. - Consequences: the old layout disappears as the steps run, and nothing is lost. - Related: AC-0018-0007, retired BR, retired BR, retired BR | DONE |

| DEC-0390 | .qfai/spec/spec-0018/07_Decisions.md#DR-0018-0013: rules cite their CLI contract in the rule text | - Status: accepted - Context: `Contract-Refs` traces only API, database and UI contracts, and this spec follows CLI contracts. - Decision: write `-` in `Contract-Refs` and name the contract file and section in each rule's `Rule` cell. - Decision, rejected alternative: short contract IDs in `Contract-Refs`, which no tool traces here (the author's recommendation). - Related: `04_Business-Rules.md` § `Reference Column Conventions` ## Re-open records `Status: re-open` is the `[RE-OPEN]` decision record the Delta Rejected Guard (`.qfai/assistant/constitution/shared-skill-operating-baseline.md`) requires before a candidate listed under a delta's `## Rejected` may be re-adopted. It is an ordinary entry in this file, so it inherits the ID scheme above and resolves the same way. A re-open entry carries three things beyond a normal decision: - `Re-opens:` — the prior `DR-*` being reconsidered. It must be a declared ID, and it cannot be the entry's own nor a re-open that points back at it: a pair citing each other has no prior decision anywhere in the loop. - `Decision:` — what changed since the rejection. A re-open that repeats the original argument is the reintroduction the guard exists to stop, and the sample block's own `<...>` prompt counts as unwritten. - `Approved by:` / `Approved at:` — the explicit approval, the time as `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ`. Until both are filled, the entry stays `Status: proposed`. The rejected candidate in the same spec's delta points back at it through `## Rejected`'s `Re-opened by:` line. Both directions are required, so the rejection and the re-adoption are readable from either end. `npx qfai validate` reports `QFAI-DECISION-001` when the entry's own ID is off the scheme or `Re-opens:` is missing, malformed, self-referential or circular, `QFAI-DECISION-002` when it resolves to no declared record, `QFAI-DECISION-003` when the approval is absent or `Approved at:` is not a real `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ` instant, `QFAI-DECISION-004` when the delta's `Re-opened by:` and this entry do not name each other, `QFAI-DECISION-005` when `Decision:` is missing, `QFAI-DECISION-006` when a candidate the delta lists under `## Rejected` reappears under `## Adopted` with no `Re-opened by:` of its own, and `QFAI-DECISION-007` when the same `DR-*` is declared twice in this file, which leaves the re-opened decision ambiguous. A re-open asserted anywhere else — a PR description, a commit message — is not one. | DONE |

| DEC-0412 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0012-001: Blocking authority of the total-negation agent and its demotion to advisory | - Decision: Grant the total-negation agent (devils-advocate) blocking FAIL authority, and demote it to advisory after 3 consecutive FAILs - Context: If the total-negation agent keeps issuing blocking FAILs without limit, an infinite loop in which the skill never completes may occur - Rationale: Blocking FAIL authority achieves strict review, while demotion to advisory after 3 consecutive FAILs prevents the infinite loop. Temptation: Wanting to maximize quality | DONE |

Do not demand numeric targets or more BR, non-functional floors, policies, decisions or architecture. - Context: Concrete coverage gaps can occur in any skill's artifacts. Independently required gates, product obligations and the whole safety floor in `.agents/rules/minimal-implementation.md` § 2 still apply. - Authority: `.qfai/assistant/catalog/review-gate.rules.yml` bounds this mode, including targets in preserved `review-profiles.yml` manifests. Temptation: counts make review easy to measure. - Rejected-B: SDD-only review leaves concrete coverage gaps in other skills. - DO NOT: Restrict this optional mode to SDD. Temptation: other skills do not always produce concrete artifacts, but those runs can return N/A. - Related: `CR-20260913-0007`. | DONE |

| DEC-0539 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0111: Strict Classification Validation — contradiction-detection gate (v1.7.14) | - Decision: Newly add readValidatedClassificationBlock() and make semantic contradictions inside the classification block (ui_bearing=false + non-empty secondary_surfaces, ui_bearing=true + primary_surface=non-ui and so on) a hard error - Context: In v1.7.13, readClassificationBlock() only returned the parse result, and each validator performed the contradiction checks individually - Rationale: Eliminate the risk of production paths such as execution.ts continuing to operate on an invalid classification. Consolidate contradiction detection into a common gate in the parser layer so that all consumers receive consistent strict validation - Rejected-A: Keep the individual validator checks (duplicate implementation and the risk of inconsistency) - DO NOT: Do not use readClassificationBlock() (non-strict) in the execution path. Temptation: There may be cases where strict validation is too heavy | DONE |
| DEC-0540 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0112: Namespaced-Only Schema — legacy top-level keys hard-reject (v1.7.14) | - Decision: If legacy top-level recommendation keys of prototyping.yaml (recommended_mode, allowed_modes and so on) exist, it is a hard error regardless of whether a namespaced `prototyping:` block exists - Context: In the existence-based precedence of v1.7.13 (DR-0283), the namespaced block took priority but legacy keys were tolerated as a warning (QFAI-PROT-231/232) - Rationale: As a current-only SSOT release, structurally prohibit the very existence of the legacy schema. The warning→error promotion clearly ends the migration period - Rejected-A: Keep the warning and promote to error in v1.8.0 (extending the migration delays convergence) - DO NOT: Do not tolerate the existence of legacy top-level keys with a warning. Temptation: Wanting to soften the impact on existing projects | DONE |
| DEC-0541 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0113: Semantic Invariant SSOT — recommended_mode ∈ allowed_modes (v1.7.14) | - Decision: Newly add validateRecommendationSemantics() in recommendationSemantics.ts and make it the SSOT shared across all layers, validator/runtime/execution/CLI, for the requirement that recommended_mode is included in allowed_modes (QFAI-PROT-154) - Context: In v1.7.13, the semantic mismatch check existed only in the validator (prototypingRecommendation.ts), and the execution/CLI paths were unverified - Rationale: A gap in verifying a semantic invariant leads directly to a runtime error. Make the shared helper the single source of truth, and have all layers, the parser (extractRecommendation), resolver, execution, CLI, validator and preflight, refer to the same logic - Rejected-A: Add individual checks to execution.ts (duplicate implementation, risk of inconsistency) - DO NOT: Do not implement the semantic invariant check anywhere other than the helper. Temptation: Writing it inline in each layer is quicker | DONE |
| DEC-0542 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0114: Canonical Strategy Decision Vocabulary (v1.7.14) | - Decision: Introduce a canonical enum (template, component-library, design-system, native-pattern, bespoke, none) for the strategy decision fields (decision, chosen_option, candidate_options) and prohibit free-form text - Context: In v1.7.13, the strategy validator did only structural checks on 8 fields, and the value of decision was an arbitrary string - Rationale: A canonical vocabulary enables comparison, aggregation and automated analysis of strategy decisions. Enforcing the state machine selection_required=true → ≥2 candidates + non-"none" decision, and selection_required=false → decision="none", guarantees semantic consistency - Rejected-A: Allow free-form and make the enum only a recommendation (comparison and aggregation would be difficult) - DO NOT: Do not allow values outside the canonical enum in the strategy decision fields. Temptation: Wanting to enter project-specific options freely | DONE |
| DEC-0543 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0115: Current-Only SSOT — complete removal of migration/defer wording (v1.7.14) | - Decision: Completely remove wording such as v2.0 defer, legacy deprecation, reconsidered-in-v2.0 and migration guide from steering documents such as product.md and manifest.md - Context: The steering docs up to v1.7.13 had remnants of the migration period, such as "reconsider in v2.0" and "legacy is deprecated" - Rationale: v1.7.14 is a current-only SSOT release. Shipped documents describe only the current specification and exclude mentions of future migration or past compatibility. This eliminates the risk of document readers misunderstanding the migration status - Rejected-A: Keep the migration history as an appendix (goes against the current-only principle) - DO NOT: Do not reintroduce migration/defer/reconsidered wording into steering/product/manifest. Temptation: Wanting to keep the history | DONE |
| DEC-0544 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0116: Independent Evaluator Panel 3-Layer Structure (v1.7.14) | - Decision: Introduce a 3-layer independent evaluation panel into the iterative improvement loop of full-harness mode. L1: product-surface-reviewer (UI/UX design quality), L2: product-experience-architect (product experience), L3: qa-gatekeeper (process audit) - Context: Two incident reports confirmed a self-evaluation bias in which the generator evaluates itself and over-reports quality scores. Cases occurred where scoringTrace scores were judged converged without improvement, and where the invocation of an independent reviewer was faked with fabricated names - Rationale: Launch L1/L2 in separate contexts with the task tool's background mode and exclude the improvement history, previous scores and generator plan from their input, structurally eliminating bias. weightedTotal is the minimum of L1/L2, so a high score from only one does not lead to accept. product-experience-architect is kind: worker, so it is placed in the evidence phase of agent-routing.yml rather than in review-profiles.yml - Rejected-A: Evaluation by a single reviewer (multi-perspective evaluation is impossible and blind spots remain) - DO NOT: Do not run the iteration evaluation of full-harness with a single agent. Temptation: Thinking one reviewer is enough - Rejected-B: Register product-experience-architect in always_required of review-profiles.yml (the QFAI-AGENT-010 validator rejects it because it is kind: worker) - DO NOT: Do not register a kind: worker agent in review-profiles.yml. Temptation: Wanting to manage all evaluators uniformly in the review profile | DONE |
| DEC-0545 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0117: Score Scope Separation — Discussion ≠ Prototyping (v1.7.14) | - Decision: Clearly separate the discussion 3-layer aggregate scores (design direction quality) from the prototyping scoringTrace (implementation fidelity), and prohibit copying - Context: An incident report confirmed a case where the aggregate scores at discussion completion were copied as-is into the prototyping scoringTrace, and no independent evaluation of implementation quality was performed. As a result, all iterations were falsely judged converged with the same score - Rationale: Discussion scores measure "which design direction best satisfies the evaluation criteria" (what), and prototyping scores measure "how good the implementation quality is against the chosen anchor" (how well). The evaluation targets differ fundamentally, so reusing scores is semantically invalid - Rejected-A: Use the discussion scores as the initial values of prototyping (because the evaluation targets differ, they are inappropriate even as initial values) - DO NOT: Do not use the discussion aggregate scores as initial or reference values of the prototyping scoringTrace. Temptation: Wanting prototyping to start from a high score if discussion scored high | DONE |
| DEC-0546 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0200: converged requires iterationCount>=2 (v1.7.15) | - Decision: The converged judgment requires iterationCount >= 2, and plateauLookback >= 2 is enforced in the CalibrationLoader schema - Status: Adopted | TODO |
| DEC-0547 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0201: Reviewer placeholder reject list frozen (v1.7.15) | - Decision: Freeze the reviewer placeholder reject list at the 6 values "qfai", "default", "auto", "system", "unknown" and "". The resolvedReviewer ?? "qfai" fallback is prohibited - Status: Adopted | TODO |
| DEC-0548 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0202: commitSha mandatory in full-harness (v1.7.15) | - Decision: commitSha is mandatory when running full-harness, and it is a runtime error when it cannot be obtained - Status: Adopted | TODO |
| DEC-0549 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0203: packVersion from pack metadata only (v1.7.15) | - Decision: packVersion is obtained dynamically from the pack metadata via CalibrationLoader. Hard-coding is prohibited - Status: Adopted | TODO |
| DEC-0550 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0204: weightedTotal = min(l1.total, l2.total) always (v1.7.15) | - Decision: computeWeightedTotal always returns Math.min(l1.total, l2.total) - Status: Adopted | TODO |
| DEC-0551 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0205: specCoverage from real diffs only (v1.7.15) | - Decision: specCoverage is derived from real spec/runtime evidence. Zero-seeded output is prohibited - Status: Adopted | TODO |
| DEC-0552 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0206: uiFidelity observation-only (v1.7.15) | - Decision: uiFidelity is composed only from DOM parse / browser QA / render evidence. A synthetic mockPaths pass is prohibited - Status: Adopted | TODO |
| DEC-0553 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0207: CalibrationLoader wired in execution.ts (v1.7.15) | - Decision: CalibrationLoader is called in execution.ts after loadConfig() (not in config.ts) - Status: Adopted | TODO |
| DEC-0554 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0208: Fail-fast no silent fallback (v1.7.15) | - Decision: When required evidence is missing, fail immediately with a runtime error. Filling in default values is prohibited - Status: Adopted | TODO |
| DEC-0555 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0209: Pre-scored l1/l2 path elimination (v1.7.15 rev2) | - Decision: Remove l1/l2 from the request type of runFullHarness(). Scoring is executed centrally inside the runtime. Throw immediately when panelInputs is missing - Context: There was a path where request.l1/l2 accepted values pre-scored externally and the runtime skipped scoring. As a result, scores that are not evidence-grounded were used for the converged judgment - Rationale: Confining the only path of scoring inside the runtime structurally prevents deviation from evidence - Rejected: Keep request.l1/l2 as optional (it becomes a breeding ground for silent bypass) - DO NOT: Do not leave a pre-scored path in the request type. Temptation: Wanting to make it optional for backward compatibility - Status: Adopted | TODO |
| DEC-0556 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0210: l2Evidence.ts new file for real artifact derivation (v1.7.15 rev2) | - Decision: Newly add l2Evidence.ts in packages/qfai/src/core/prototyping/. Derive the L2 input from real artifacts with buildDiscussionAxisInputs / buildScreenContractInputs / buildTrendAlignmentInputs - Context: An L2 dummy object (aggregateScore:0, evidenceRefs:[]) was generated inline in execution.ts - Rationale: Consolidate the reading of real artifacts into a dedicated module and prevent the dummy object from recurring. Throw when evidence is insufficient - Rejected: Add the build functions inline in execution.ts (blurs the module's responsibility) - DO NOT: Do not embed the L2 evidence derivation in execution.ts. Temptation: Wanting to finish in one file - Status: Adopted | TODO |
| DEC-0557 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0211: CalibrationLoader fail-open removal (v1.7.15 rev2) | - Decision: Remove all fail-open paths of CalibrationLoader. Abolish the DEFAULT_PACK fallback / filling in version="1.0.0" / injecting default values when thresholds are missing - Context: Because it could continue with DEFAULT_PACK even when the pack was absent, a full-harness run without calibration was possible - Rationale: A fail-closed design structurally guarantees the existence and validity of the calibration pack - Rejected: Keep DEFAULT_PACK as a safe default only when the pack is absent (it would become the last bastion of fail-open) - DO NOT: Do not leave a fallback in CalibrationLoader. Temptation: Wanting to reduce friction in the first-time setup - Status: Adopted | TODO |
| DEC-0558 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0212: TerminationContext receives CalibrationPack only (v1.7.15 rev2) | - Decision: computeTerminationReason() / computeStatus() in history.ts receive { calibration: CalibrationPack; history: FullHarnessHistory }. Resolving plateauLookback from anywhere other than the pack is abolished - Status: Adopted | TODO |
| DEC-0559 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0213: Screen-level UiObservation with ScreenObservation type (v1.7.15 rev2) | - Decision: Rebuild UiObservationSummary based on ScreenObservation[]. Abolish the flatten aggregation and keep observation results at the screen level - Context: Because the DOM labels / actions / mockPaths of all screens were flattened and aggregated, per-screen quality judgment was impossible - Rationale: Keeping them at the screen level makes it possible to detect insufficient-evidence for individual screens. uiFidelityBuilder also builds observed per screen - Rejected: Keep the flatten aggregation and add a screen breakdown inside the summary (a double structure) - DO NOT: Do not let the flatten aggregation and the screen level coexist. Temptation: Wanting to keep both for backward compatibility - Status: Adopted | TODO |
| DEC-0560 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0214: bundleWriter schema v2 only (v1.7.15 rev2) | - Decision: bundleWriter outputs only schema v2 (8-category evidenceRefs + the new FullHarnessIteration type). Coexistence of v1/v2 is prohibited - Status: Adopted | TODO |
| DEC-0561 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0215: Validator 14-rule error upgrade (v1.7.15 rev2) | - Decision: Promote the 14 items of prototypingEvidence.ts from warning to error. Semantic changes that are new are split off into new rule IDs - Status: Adopted | TODO |
| DEC-0562 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0216: DB coverage binary policy (v1.7.15 rev2) | - Decision: When there are declared DB objects but no observation, it is a full-harness failure. "Continue while always treating as missing" is prohibited - Status: Adopted | TODO |
| DEC-0563 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0217: cli/full-harness reject at 4 layers (v1.7.15 rev4) | - Decision: Reject the combination of `cli` + `full-harness` at 4 layers: the CLI / derivePrototypingObligations / runFullHarness / the validator - Status: Adopted - Rationale: Running full-harness on a non-UI surface only runs a meaningless Browser QA cycle. Extended from 3 layers (rev2 DR-0210) to 4 layers - Alternatives: (A) Reject at the CLI layer only — insufficient, can be bypassed / (B) 4-layer defense (adopted) - Source: discussion-20260414195449523, WS-1 | TODO |
| DEC-0564 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0218: screen contract-based Browser QA targets (v1.7.15 rev4) | - Decision: Change the Browser QA targets from the fixed value `"/primary"` to dynamic derivation based on the screen definitions in `40_screen_contracts.md` - Status: Adopted - Rationale: A fixed value caused missed measurements of multiple screens, which an audit detected as a discrepancy - Alternatives: (A) Keep "/primary" — missed measurements / (B) Screen contract derivation (adopted) - Source: discussion-20260414195449523, WS-2 | TODO |
| DEC-0565 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0219: Browser QA evidence chain hard-fail on empty (v1.7.15 rev4) | - Decision: When `iterations[].evidenceRefs.browserQa` is empty, it is a hard fail and a silent pass is prohibited - Status: Adopted - Rationale: An interrupted evidence chain means audit trails cannot be followed. Part of the fail-closed policy - Alternatives: (A) Continue even when empty — breaks the audit chain / (B) Hard fail (adopted) - Source: discussion-20260414195449523, WS-3 | TODO |
| DEC-0566 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0220: canonical route semantics for runtimeGate/specCoverage (v1.7.15 rev4) | - Decision: In `runtimeGateBuilder.ts` / `specCoverage.ts`, compare by canonical path (the normalized path) and not by URL - Status: Adopted - Rationale: Eliminate the bug in which a URL containing query parameters or a fragment was mistakenly judged to be a different route - Alternatives: (A) Use the URL as is — misjudgment / (B) Canonical path comparison (adopted) - Source: discussion-20260414195449523, WS-4 | TODO |
| DEC-0567 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0221: L2 structured parse priority over heuristic (v1.7.15 rev4) | - Decision: In L2 evidence collection, prioritize structured parsing (the 20-23 series, 04_Sources.md, 40_screen_contracts.md), and allow the heuristic fallback only when no structured source exists - Status: Adopted - Rationale: Relying on heuristics lowers evidence accuracy and reproducibility - Alternatives: (A) Heuristic first — lower accuracy / (B) Structured parse first (adopted) - Source: discussion-20260414195449523, WS-5 | TODO |
| DEC-0568 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0222: parameterized route pattern-based matching (v1.7.15 rev4, retired OQ resolution) | - Decision: Adopt pattern-based matching (Option B) for matching parameterized Browser QA routes (e.g., `/orders/:id`) - Status: Adopted - Rationale: With exact match only, the Browser QA evidence chain for dynamic routes breaks. Canonical normalization is over-engineering - Alternatives: (A) Exact match only — no support for dynamic routes / (B) Pattern-based matching (adopted) / (C) Canonical normalization — excessive complexity - Source: discussion-20260414195449523, retired OQ | TODO |
| DEC-0569 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0223: ui[] row validation inline in prototypingEvidence.ts (v1.7.15 rev9, retired OQ resolution) | - Decision: Implement the validation of the 3 row-level fields of `runtimeGate.ui[]` (declaredRef/renderEvidenceRefs[]/browserQaEvidenceRefs[]) inline within `prototypingEvidence.ts` (Option A) - Status: Adopted - Rationale: Design doc §6-1-2 names `prototypingEvidence.ts` as a changed file. Extracting a small, cohesive validation unit into a separate module has no architectural benefit. Inline preserves cohesion - Alternatives: (A) inline in prototypingEvidence.ts (adopted) / (B) extract validateRuntimeGateUiRow() to separate utility — unnecessary module split - Source: discussion-20260416092414328, retired OQ | TODO |
| DEC-0570 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0224: browserQaEvidenceRefs[] always required non-empty (v1.7.15 rev9, retired OQ resolution) | - Decision: `runtimeGate.ui[].browserQaEvidenceRefs[]` is always required non-empty even when "browser QA was not performed", and an empty array is a hard fail (Option A) - Status: Adopted - Rationale: The fail-closed policy of design doc §3-2. Consistent with the precedent of rejecting an empty `runtimeGate.evidenceRefs` array in the rev8 retired OQ. Allowing empty creates a loophole where the builder outputs empty and the validator passes it - Alternatives: (A) always required non-empty (adopted) / (B) allow empty when no browser QA run — violates fail-closed - Source: discussion-20260416092414328, retired OQ | TODO |
| DEC-0571 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0225: per-axis evidenceRefs validation granularity (v1.7.15 rev9, retired OQ resolution) | - Decision: Validate `fullHarness.iterations[].l1/l2.axes[].evidenceRefs[]` at per-axis granularity (Option A). If any axis has an empty array, it is a validator error - Status: Adopted - Rationale: Conforms to the per-element description of design doc §6-1-3. Allowing aggregate leniency (an error only when all axes are empty) would let some axes pass without evidence - Alternatives: (A) per-axis validation (adopted) / (B) aggregate leniency — breaks the per-axis traceability contract - Source: discussion-20260416092414328, retired OQ | TODO |
| DEC-0572 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0226: full README enumeration of all concrete-ref leaf fields (v1.7.15 rev9, retired OQ resolution) | - Decision: State all leaf fields of the concrete-ref contract in the README (ui[].declaredRef, ui[].renderEvidenceRefs[], ui[].browserQaEvidenceRefs[], axes[].evidenceRefs[], reviewerLogs[].evidenceRefs[]) (Option A) - Status: Adopted - Rationale: DoD §5-6 "make docs/validator partial-strictness mismatches zero" is a hard gate. Design doc §9 explicitly prohibits "weakening the README's wording to make them agree" - Alternatives: (A) full enumeration (adopted) / (B) minimal note — violates DoD §5-6 - Source: discussion-20260416092414328, retired OQ | TODO |
| DEC-0573 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0227: UI-bearing discussion requires design guideline research (v1.7.17) | - Decision: In a UI-bearing discussion, design guideline research is a mandatory step in addition to Trend Scan. Include at least 1 line of references suited to the project context, such as Material Design / WCAG / Apple HIG / platform/library guidelines - Status: Adopted - Rationale: The root cause of visual quality failures is missing upstream research, not prototyping, so it must be closed in discussion - Alternatives: (A) Correct after the fact in the prototyping skill — cannot close the root cause / (B) Make it a discussion mandatory step (adopted) - Source: discussion-20260418170937652, DR-001 | TODO |
| DEC-0574 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0228: `design_guideline_research` becomes canonical Trend Scan category (v1.7.17) | - Decision: Add `design_guideline_research` to the canonical categories of `04_Sources.md` - Status: Adopted - Rationale: Putting guideline evidence on the same traceability surface as the existing source registry lets the validator and downstream specs refer to the same SSOT - Alternatives: (A) Create a separate file — category drift / (B) Integrate into 04_Sources (adopted) - Source: discussion-20260418170937652, DR-002 | TODO |
| DEC-0575 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0229: Trend-derived `score_anchors` require quantitative proxy and warning-first rollout (v1.7.17) | - Decision: The `score_anchors` of the legacy trend-derived scoring artifact prohibit abstract adjectives alone and must include at least one quantitative proxy such as a px value / ratio / rule ID / class name / library default. The validator severity is warning in v1.7.17 - Status: Adopted - Rationale: An anchor without concreteness lets a low-quality UI through even with a high score. On the other hand, a staged rollout is appropriate given the impact on existing packs - Alternatives: (A) Immediate error — migration shock / (B) warning-first ratchet (adopted) - Source: discussion-20260418170937652, DR-003 / retired OQ resolution | TODO |
| DEC-0576 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0230: Validator ownership split = trendScan coverage + scoringReady concreteness (v1.7.17) | - Decision: The guideline coverage validator extends `packages/qfai/src/core/validators/uix/trendScan.ts`, and the anchor concreteness validator extends `packages/qfai/src/core/validators/uix/scoringReady.ts`. No new top-level validator is added - Status: Adopted - Rationale: Category completeness is the responsibility of the sources schema and anchor concreteness that of the scoring-ready schema, which matches the current canonical validator boundaries - Alternatives: (A) A new top-level validator — blurs the ownership split / (B) Extend the existing uix modules (adopted) - Source: discussion-20260418170937652, DR-004 / retired OQ resolution | TODO |
| DEC-0577 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0231: Make Brave Search MCP the primary search provider (v1.8.0) | - Decision: Adopt Brave Search as the primary search MCP of Web Research Enhancement - Status: Adopted - Rationale: It has the best balance of community adoption, documentation and ease of integration with CLI agents - Alternatives: (A) Make Tavily primary / (B) Make multiple providers primary on an equal footing - Source: discussion-20260328212829687, retired OQ | TODO |
| DEC-0578 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0232: Document both the hosted and local npx modes of Firecrawl, and recommend local for sensitive environments (v1.8.0) | - Decision: The Firecrawl integration provides both a hosted URL and a local `npx` configuration, and recommends local for sensitive environments - Status: Adopted - Rationale: Both security and ease of adoption are needed, and fixing a single mode does not meet operational requirements - Alternatives: (A) hosted only / (B) local only - Source: discussion-20260328212829687, retired OQ | TODO |
| DEC-0579 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0233: SSE transport is out of scope for v1.8.0 and deferred to post-v1.8.0 (v1.8.0) | - Decision: The MCP transports in scope are only stdio and HTTP, and SSE-based integration is not handled in v1.8.0 - Status: Adopted - Rationale: Given the Apify SSE deprecation, formally adopting SSE at this point carries high maintenance cost and uncertainty - Alternatives: (A) Include SSE in v1.8.0 / (B) Leave it ambiguous without a per-transport policy - Source: discussion-20260328212829687, retired OQ | TODO |
| DEC-0580 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0234: Fix content sanitization at moderate scope (v1.8.0) | - Decision: The sanitizer is limited to removing control chars, `aria-hidden` and `display:none`, and does no ML-based judgment or excessive removal - Status: Adopted - Rationale: Moderate scope is the best balance between security measures and content fidelity - Alternatives: (A) basic only / (B) aggressive semantic sanitization - Source: discussion-20260328212829687, retired OQ | TODO |
| DEC-0581 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0235: The evaluation harness stays at metrics definitions and is not fixed to a specific tool (v1.8.0) | - Decision: The common specification for evaluation goes only as far as defining the metrics of citation precision, coverage, freshness and security hygiene, and is not fixed to a specific vendor/evaluation tool - Status: Adopted - Rationale: Keep the evaluation foundation replaceable while sharing only the viewpoint of the quality gate - Alternatives: (A) Make a specific evaluation tool mandatory / (B) Do not define the metrics themselves - Source: discussion-20260328212829687, retired OQ | TODO |
| DEC-0582 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0236: Research sub-agents adopt conservative defaults (v1.8.0) | - Decision: The defaults of the research sub-agents are `max_threads=2` and `max_depth=2`, and higher values are an explicit opt-in - Status: Adopted - Rationale: Prevent runaway parallelism and search depth, and keep a balance among rate limits, cost and traceability - Alternatives: (A) No limit / (B) Fixed at 1 - Source: discussion-20260328212829687, retired OQ | TODO |
| DEC-0583 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0237: The cache staleness threshold defaults to 24 hours and can be overridden by config (v1.8.0) | - Decision: The default stale threshold of the research cache is 24 hours and can be overridden in settings - Status: Adopted - Rationale: It is a practical balance between freshness and API cost, and differences between use cases can be absorbed by config - Alternatives: (A) A fixed value with no override / (B) Disable the cache - Source: discussion-20260328212829687, retired OQ | TODO |

| DEC-0588 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0250: DR-0250..0260: CHG-003 — Assistant-layer Recut + Work-log Surface (2026-05-22) | Source: discussion-20260522081618995 retired OQ (10 resolved, 2 deferred). #### DR-0250: Promotion target is the per-spec `07_Decisions.md` alone (retired OQ resolved) - Decision: The promote target of a `kind: decision` work-log entry is only the per-spec `07_Decisions.md`. Per-spec scope is expressed with the frontmatter `scope: spec-NNNN`. - Rationale: Avoid per-spec path proliferation. Cross-spec memos can also be expressed in frontmatter. - Rejected option: Also providing a per-spec `.qfai/specs/spec-NNNN/steering/` (because of path proliferation). - Source: user via AskUserQuestion 2026-05-22. #### DR-0253: Relocate `spec_required_files.json` to catalog/ (retired OQ resolved) - Decision: Move the existing `.qfai/assistant/manifest/spec_required_files.json` to `.qfai/assistant/catalog/`. The new Manifest layer is dedicated to the project spine. - Rationale: A registry artifact is the Catalog's responsibility and is separated from the Manifest (project spine). - Rejected option: Leave it in the old `manifest/` (conflicts with the meaning of the new Manifest). - Source: user via AskUserQuestion 2026-05-22. #### DR-0254: `.qfai/steering/` is excluded by default in `.gitignore` (retired OQ resolved) - Decision: The work-log surface is untracked by default. A project that opts in can commit it with a `.gitignore` override. - Rationale: Defense-in-depth against accidental secret commits. Teams that want a shared resume context can opt in. - Rejected option: Tracked by default (risk of secret leaks). - Source: requirements-analyst, SRC-0001. #### DR-0255: The deprecation window for the old paths is 1 minor release (retired OQ resolved) - Decision: The validator accepts the old layout and the new layout in parallel for 1 minor release and emits a `D-DEPRECATED-PATH` warning. In the next minor, acceptance of the old paths is removed and the warning escalates to an error. - Rationale: Consistent with the past ATDD migration cadence (`process/migrations/v1.4.27-atdd-alignment.md`). - Rejected option: A hard cut (removing acceptance of the old paths within 1 release; a large break for consumers). - Source: requirements-analyst, prior migration memo. #### DR-0256: Work-log entries use YAML frontmatter (retired OQ resolved) - Decision: The metadata of `.qfai/steering/*.md` is YAML frontmatter. - Rationale: Consistent with the existing `qfai-*` SKILL.md convention. It also pairs well with prose fields such as `closure-rationale`. - Rejected option: TOML (thin tool ecosystem), JSON (needs separation from the prose body). - Source: requirements-analyst, SRC-0009. #### DR-0257: Entry filename = `<id>.md`, where `id` is kebab-case ASCII (retired OQ resolved) - Decision: Make the filename stem match the frontmatter `id`. - Rationale: Chronological order in `ls`, unique enough, human-readable. - Rejected option: UUID filenames (low human readability), `YYYY-MM-DD/<slug>.md` (more per-day directories). - Source: requirements-analyst, SRC-0001. #### DR-0258: Reviewer drift findings are severity error + mandatory justification (advisory-failing) (retired OQ resolved) - Decision: `R-WORKLOG-DRIFT` / `R-REJECTED-READOPT` are severity error but require a non-empty `justification:` field. `qfai validate` rejects an `R-*` finding that lacks a justification. - Rationale: Making natural-language heuristic drift detection a hard block would destroy trust through false positives. Making it warning-only would get it ignored. Advisory-failing takes the middle path. - Rejected option: warning-only (ignored); hard-block (trust destroyed by false positives). - Source: requirements-analyst, SRC-0001. #### DR-0259: `D-DEPRECATED-PATH` is a warning during the window / an error from sunset (retired OQ resolved) - Decision: A warning during the window, and it escalates to an error at the sunset version. The warning text names the sunset version every time (NFR-0003). - Rationale: An error on day 1 bricks installed copies. Warning-only is ignored. A version-aware phased migration is safe. - Rejected option: An error on day 1 (consumers' installed copies would stop working). - Source: requirements-analyst, SRC-0001. #### DR-0260: AGENTS.md alignment and auto-archival are deferred (retired OQ + retired OQ deferred) - Decision: The AGENTS.md / `CLAUDE.md` symlink discussion is split off into a separate `/qfai-discussion` invocation (target 2026-09-30). Automatic archival of `.qfai/steering/` is substituted by the `W-WORKLOG-STALE` surface of `qfai validate` until the post-v1 dogfooding review (target 2026-12-31). - Rationale: The two have independent discovery scopes. Bundling them into this pack would exceed atomicity. - Source: requirements-analyst, the deferred row in `13_Deferred.md`. | DONE |

Trace: discussion-20260527075558258 retired OQ (Spec I). #### DR-0269: SKILL.md Default Autopilot Policy template — 3 named buckets (retired OQ resolved) - Date: 2026-05-27 - Statement: Every SKILL.md `## Default Autopilot Policy` section uses three named buckets. (a) **auto-decide** (named defaults, AI decides without prompting): output formatting, ID / sequence numbering, append-vs-create when subject overlaps an existing artifact, and option-pick among demonstrably-equivalent alternatives. (b) **ask-user** (AI prompts via AskUserQuestion): approval-required triage ops (CREATE / DELETE / SPLIT / MERGE / SUPERSEDE / UPDATE:REMOVE), destructive operations, version-pin changes, and scope expansions. (c) **hard-required** (no default possible; must be supplied before proceeding): brand intent, `primarySpecId` when absent. The three enumerations are the prototype: a skill MAY narrow ANY of the three buckets (drop an entry it cannot reach) but MUST NOT widen one. Only auto-decide widening is machine-detectable (its entry set is closed) and surfaces `R-AUTOPILOT-POLICY-WIDENED` (warning); ask-user / hard-required are enforced by review. Reviewer Gate emits `R-AUTOPILOT-POLICY-MISSING` (error) when the section is absent. - Amendment (2026-08-22): the narrowing permission originally covered auto-decide only, so `/qfai-implement` shipped `/qfai-sdd`'s triage ops in ask-user and init's branding inputs in hard-required — decisions and inputs an implement run never reaches. Narrowing now applies to all three buckets; widening stays forbidden in all three. - Amendment 2 (2026-08-22): narrowing alone left `/qfai-implement` with no legal way to name the authorizations it DOES need. Its `TDDLIST-001` accepted-risk waiver and its Drift-Protocol Change-Request escalation are the same kind of decision as `/qfai-sdd`'s triage ops — a human authorization the skill cannot grant itself — but neither is a triage op, so listing them read as widening. **The ask-user bucket's first entry is therefore a category, not a fixed op list: _approval-required governance operations_, which each skill instantiates with the operations its own run requires human authorization for.** `/qfai-sdd` instantiates it as the triage ops (CREATE / DELETE / SPLIT / MERGE / SUPERSEDE / UPDATE:REMOVE); `/qfai-implement` instantiates it as the `TDDLIST-001` waiver approval and the Change-Request escalation. Instantiating a category with the skill's own operations is **not** widening; introducing a **new category** is, and stays forbidden. The other three ask-user entries (destructive operations, version-pin changes, scope expansions) were already category-shaped and are unchanged. - Amendment 4 (2026-09-12): narrowing the buckets to the operations a skill performs left the interview skills with no legal entry. `/qfai-grilling` and `/qfai-grill` perform the asking itself: a frontier decision and the confirmation that closes a session are what those runs do, and neither is a triage op, a destructive operation, a version pin or a scope expansion — so listing them read as widening. **The ask-user bucket gains a fifth category: _a decision a declared grilling session puts to the user_, available only to a skill whose own operation is the interview.** A skill that runs a session inside some other operation does not instantiate it: the session's questions are the session's, and `.agents/rules/grilling.md` owns which are asked. The category is closed the way the first one is — instantiating it with the skill's own questions is not widening, and a new category still is. - Amendment 3 (2026-09-07): the hard-required bucket is machine-checked as well. `QFAI-AUTOPILOT-001` reads every shipped `qfai-*` SKILL.md and reports a bucket naming an entry this decision has retired, or one no skill declares — a warning until the 1.12.0 release and an error from there. The statement above says only auto-decide widening is detectable because its entry set is closed; hard-required's is closed too, by the common entries plus a per-skill declaration, so the same reading applies. `companyName` is the retired entry: no shipped file read it, so the bucket paid a guaranteed prompt out of a 0-1 budget and read nothing back. ask-user remains enforced by review — its first entry is a category each skill instantiates, which no closed set describes. - Chosen option: per-category opinionated template (register option C) with the three buckets above as the prototype. - Rejected option A — conservative (most decisions ask user): preserves the 3–6 avoidable `AskUserQuestion` per session that this pack exists to remove. - DO NOT: default to asking on procedural decisions. Temptation: maximize governance. - Rejected option B — aggressive (most decisions auto-decide): erodes governance by auto-deciding triage / destructive / scope / version operations that require human authorization. - DO NOT: auto-decide approval-required or destructive operations. Temptation: maximize autopilot. - Source REQ: REQ-0160. Trace: discussion-20260527075558258 retired OQ (Spec H). #### DR-0270: Envelope-deviation `AskUserQuestion` audit trigger taxonomy (retired OQ resolved) - Date: 2026-05-27 - Statement: The audit-log write (REQ-0158) triggers when an `AskUserQuestion` template names any of the four envelope-deviation contexts: "skill envelope", "architectural decision", "rejected-option re-adoption", or "scope expansion". On trigger, the skill body writes `.qfai/evidence/decisions/<ISO8601-ts>.json` `{question, answer, scope, operatorIdentity, timestamp, envelopeContractClause}`. (This is the register's option C — a per-skill declared list of envelope contexts — pinned to a fixed four-context taxonomy so the trigger is deterministic and reviewable rather than a heuristic regex.) `.qfai/evidence/decisions/` is tracked in version control (governance record; negated in the managed `.gitignore` block). - Chosen option: fixed four-context declared taxonomy (register option C, pinned). - Rejected option A — explicit `AskUserQuestion({envelopeDeviation: true})` parameter: requires every skill author to remember to set the flag; a missed flag silently drops the audit record (fail-open). - DO NOT: depend on a per-call boolean flag. | DEC-0591 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0275: DR-0275..0276: CHG-007 — Layered CI Test Scaffold Adoption (2026-08-05) | Source: discussion-20260804173914356 (REQ-0001..0025, NFR-0001..0016, DTC-1..28), resolving that pack's deferred `retired OQ` (spec and capability allocation). ApprovedBy: user@2026-08-05. These two rows are the policy-layer allocation decisions the per-spec slices cite; the full change record, its Triage Table and its impact-cascade verification live in `_policies/10_delta.md` § `2026-08-05 — CHG-007`, and the two MUST stay consistent. New plain `DR-NNNN` IDs begin at DR-0275. **Six** new open questions are recorded in `_policies/09_Open-questions.md` and are NOT decided here: `retired OQ` (make the CAP-to-spec gate number-based, solution-architect), `retired OQ` (`spec-0005`'s nominal traceability chain, qa-strategist), `retired OQ` (spec-claimed implementation paths that do not exist, solution-architect) and `retired OQ` (the permanent drift blind spot for adopters who installed a shipped workflow before the provenance record existed — owner: **user**, the one user-owned question this change surfaced) and `retired OQ` (duplicate item-ID definitions inside one spec are undetected by every validator — measured on a spec this change never touched, qa-strategist) and `retired OQ`. The sixth is `retired OQ`: no validator reconciles a delta's declared ID ranges against the pack's actual contents (qa-strategist). #### DR-0275: revoke the `spec-0017` / `CAP-0017` permanent-gap reservation - Date: 2026-08-05 - Decision: the 2026-05-06 permanent-gap reservation on `spec-0017` and `CAP-0017` is revoked. Both return to being ordinary reusable IDs, and `spec-0017` is renumbered immediately as `CAP-0017 = Repository Toolchain`. - Context: `validateSpecSplitByCapability` derives its expected spec set **positionally** from the CAP count — the expected list is built by mapping each CAP's list **index** to `spec-000<index+1>` (`packages/qfai/src/core/validators/specSplitByCapability.ts:75`), so actual CAP numbers are never read. With 17 CAP rows it expects `spec-0001..spec-0017`. A 17th capability therefore had **no legal name**: `spec-0017` violated the reservation, and `spec-0018` raised `QFAI-SPLIT-103` (missing `spec-0017`) **and** `QFAI-SPLIT-104` (extra `spec-0018`) simultaneously, both at `error`. - Rationale: a reserved gap ID — at **any** position — and a positional 1:1 gate are mutually unsatisfiable from the moment the CAP count reaches that ordinal. Because the expected set only ever grows, a reservation is never permanently safe; it is only not-yet-due. The reservation was therefore not merely inconvenient but structurally unmaintainable — it blocked every future capability addition, not just this one. Renumbering is the only state that satisfies both the gate and the catalog. - Rejected: keep the reservation and name the new spec `spec-0018` - DO NOT: leave **any** gap ID reserved while the 1:1 gate is positional — a trailing reservation is not safer than an inner one, only later. Temptation: honouring a documented reservation feels like the conservative choice, but here it produces a permanently red validate. - Rejected: keep the reservation and make the validator ID-based (pair `CAP-NNNN` with `spec-NNNN` by number) in this same change - DO NOT: bundle a validator behaviour change into a spec-allocation change. Temptation: "fix the root cause once and for all" — but the validator is CAP-0004 surface with its own tests, and `08_Decisions.md` DR-0001-0005 forbids inflating a pack beyond an atomic slice. Recorded as `retired OQ` instead. - Residual risk: §ID Stability Rule 5's default (leave a gap) still contradicts the positional gate for **any** future DELETE / SUPERSEDE, wherever the gap falls, once the capability count reaches that ordinal — inner-range or trailing is irrelevant, as CHG-007 itself demonstrated (`spec-0017` was a **trailing** gap and detonated at the very next capability addition). §ID Stability Rule 5 now states this position-independently as a **rule**, not as an inner-gap exception; see `11_Slice-Policy.md` §ID Stability Rule 5. `retired OQ` tracks making the validator ID-based so the default stops being a trap. - Evidence: `packages/qfai/src/core/validators/specSplitByCapability.ts:60-131`; `_policies/11_Slice-Policy.md` §ID Stability Rule 5 + §Current Slicing Notes. - Related: `CAP-0017`, `spec-0017`, `_policies/07_Constraints.md` OC-71, `_policies/11_Slice-Policy.md`. Source REQ: REQ-0001..0025 (precondition of the allocation). Trace: discussion-20260804173914356 retired OQ. #### DR-0276: `toolchain` as a fifth slice category - Date: 2026-08-05 - Decision: add a fifth slice category `toolchain` holding the repository's own tooling — `.github/workflows/`, the repository-internal composite actions under `.github/actions/**`, root `scripts/`, `packages/qfai/scripts/`, and the test-runner configuration (`vitest.config.ts` / `vitest.workspace.ts`) — as one collective spec. `.github/actions/**` is named explicitly because `scripts/verify-pack.mjs` bans composite actions only from the **shipped** `.github` tree (`assets/init/root/.github`); repository-internal ones are legal and would otherwise be the one toolchain surface with no owner. - Context: measured against the tree, **no spec owns** `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `permissions:`, action pinning, or `vitest.workspace.ts`; all 11 root `scripts/*.mjs` are unclaimed by any pack, as is `packages/qfai/scripts/check-branch-version-pin.sh`. The four existing categories are each defined by a **distributed** product surface, so repository-internal tooling had no category. - Rationale: the gap is a category gap, not a CI gap. Filing only the CI work would leave the other orphans unowned and reproduce the same hole at the next toolchain change. - Boundary: shipped workflow templates (`assets/init/root/.github/workflows/**`) stay with **CAP-0003** (`qfai init`). Distributed-or-not is the boundary, so the two surfaces the discussion pack separates stay separated in the spec layer too. - Rejected: append the own-CI requirements to `spec-0004` - Reason: `spec-0004`'s subject is the `qfai validate` command; its implementation surface is `src/core/validators/**` + `src/cli/commands/validate.ts`, disjoint from `.github/workflows/**`. `10_delta.md:212` (do not cram different features into one spec) applies directly. - DO NOT: file GitHub Actions job topology under the validate command spec. Temptation: `spec-0004` already owns two `pnpm ci:lint` lanes, so it looks like the established home for "CI things". - Rejected: split the own-CI work across `spec-0004` (lint lane) / `spec-0009` (test config) / `spec-0011` (parallelism) - Reason: `spec-0009` scopes **adopter** repository config discovery, not QFAI's own workspace; `spec-0011`'s parallelism is agent/worktree-level, not CI-worker-level. All three would be scope escapes, and one design would be fragmented across three packs. - DO NOT: distribute one cohesive design across three specs. Temptation: every fragment individually looks like an append to something that already exists. - Consequences: `toolchain` is a collective category like `agent` — toolchain constituents do not each get their own spec. The category is repository-internal by construction, so nothing `spec-0017` owns is distributed; conversely every shipped-template requirement stays outside it and inside `CAP-0003`. - Related: `CAP-0017`, `spec-0017`, `spec-0003`, `_policies/11_Slice-Policy.md` §Slice Categories. Source REQ: REQ-0001..0013, REQ-0023, REQ-0025 (own-CI / toolchain rows); REQ-0014..0022, REQ-0024 stay on the distributed side. Trace: discussion-20260804173914356 retired OQ. | DONE |
| DEC-0592 | .qfai/spec/_policies/08_Decisions.md#DR-0277: `proseCritique` is a cap, and the unit is selected by the text | - Status: accepted - Date: 2026-09-11 - Context: `DR-0001-0003` mandated the band `200..500 words OR 600..2500 characters`. Two things in that statement are wrong about the rule QFAI-PROT-002 applies. The lower bound was removed: it failed a review for being short, which is a length a reviewer pads to reach, and it failed a review on the length of its own script rather than on what the script said. The OR was never how the unit is chosen, and choosing that way cannot work — an English critique carries no CJK characters, so it is under any character cap by construction, and a rule that passed on either unit would pass every English text however long. - Decision: `validateProseCritiqueBand` applies a **cap**, and **selects** the unit from the text. Text carrying CJK is measured in CJK characters against `PROSE_CRITIQUE_MAX_CJK_CHARS`; anything else is measured in whitespace- separated words against `PROSE_CRITIQUE_MAX_WORDS`. Only the selected unit's cap applies, and there is no lower bound in either unit. The error names the unit measured, the cap and the count. - Consequences: a critique of any length up to its cap passes, so a spec, acceptance criterion or test case stating a floor states something the code does not do. It also forecloses the English word semantic `DR-0001-0003` protected: a short English critique is no longer distinguishable from a short filler one by length, and nothing measures that. A script whose writing system separates no words and is not CJK — Thai is the clearest case — counts as very few words, so the word cap does not bind on it. That is a cap that does not apply rather than a text rejected wrongly, and binding it needs per-script segmentation. - Related: supersedes `DR-0001-0003`. `spec-0012` REQ-0012-0059, `spec-0004` REQ-0028, QFAI-PROT-002. | DONE |

| DEC-0729 | Step 9 restores an absent roster path only on a hold that shows a repair emptied it | Approved by the user on 2026-09-25, from the architecture review of step 9. A repoint moves the old link into a hold, `<link>.qfai-repair-<n>/`, before it writes the new one. A hold now means one thing: a qfai repair emptied this path and nothing has written it since. Every writer that creates a link at a path removes the holds beside it that hold a link to the old or the new target: `qfai init`, `qfai doctor` and the migration alike. A hold matches by the same name pattern prune and the gate use, not by prefix. Step 9 reads each roster path: an absent path with such a hold is restored and its hold removed; an absent path without one stays absent, even where the gate reports it missing, because the project may have removed it; a plural link is repointed; a link already naming the singular directory with a hold beside it has only the hold removed; a link naming neither directory is left as it is and listed under `## For a person` when the gate names it. A hold is removed by unlinking the link it holds and then a non-recursive `rmdir`, so a hold that gained other content keeps it and the run reports the removal as incomplete. The removal is part of the repoint: each removed hold is a target of the `repoint host integration link` operation, so the dry run lists it and the real run removes only listed holds (NFR-0002). This keeps BR-0507: restoring on a hold undoes the repair's own emptying and never recreates a wrapper the project removed, and a hold is qfai's own record rather than project content, so step 9 still repoints managed links and changes nothing else. When the platform refuses a symlink (Windows without Developer Mode), the held link goes back by `rename` while the path is empty, so a refused repoint leaves the old link in place and no hold. Related: BR-0507, AC-0004-0011-01, EX-0004-0011-01, NFR-0001, NFR-0002, `.qfai/spec/03_contract/cli/qfai-migration-spec-to-story.md`. | DONE |
| DEC-0730 | Step 9 rewrites a respelled working link, and init and doctor clear a stale hold beside a current link | Approved by the user on 2026-09-25, from the final architecture review of step 9; it extends DEC-0729. The link gate and `qfai init` judge a managed link by one rule: the target as written, normalised for the platform, must equal the target init writes. (a) A link that reaches the singular directory under another spelling, such as an absolute path or, on Windows, another letter case, is one the gate reports, so step 9 rewrites it to the gate's form the way it repoints a plural link: the old link moves into a hold first and goes back if the platform refuses the new one, and the dry run lists the rewrite. (b) A hold beside a link that is already current is left by a repair that stopped after writing the new link; `qfai init` and `qfai doctor` remove it as well, listing it in a dry run, and the migration removes only the holds its plan lists. Both stay within BR-0507 and NFR-0002. Related: DEC-0729, BR-0507, NFR-0002, `.qfai/spec/03_contract/cli/qfai-migration-spec-to-story.md`. | DONE |

| DEC-0936 | Split the stage skills into steps and route by step | - Date: 2026-09-27 - Decided by the user on 2026-09-27. - Decision: the six large stage skills `qfai-discussion`, `qfai-sdd`, `qfai-prototyping`, `qfai-verify`, `qfai-atdd` and `qfai-implement` are split into small steps, and `qfai-maintain` becomes a skill with one step, `maintain-edit`. `qfai-run`, `qfai-grill`, `qfai-grilling`, `qfai-configure`, `qfai-migration-v1-to-v2` and `web-research` are not split. - Placement: each step is `.qfai/assistant/step/<name>/STEP.md`, one level deep, named `<owner>-<name>` with no `qfai-` prefix, and is never linked into a host skill directory. A step shared by several skills has owner `common` and a `common-` name. `requires` names only common steps, and a common step requires nothing. References and templates stay under their skill. - Skills: the thirteen host-visible skills keep their names. A skill that owns steps lists them in frontmatter `steps:` and runs them one at a time, reading only the current `STEP.md`, then runs one review with the union of the reviewers of the steps it ran. Its description states only when to use it, and its `roles:` is `orchestrator` plus the union of its steps' `roles:`. The entry check and the step loop every parent follows are stated once in `.qfai/assistant/rule/shared-skill-operating-baseline.md`, and the preamble shared by every skill moves there too; each `SKILL.md` keeps its own `## Default Autopilot Policy` buckets (BR-0351). - Runs: a plan stage names an ordered list of steps, and a step may carry its own predicate. The new predicate `proposed` runs a step only when the route proposal lists it in `optionalSteps`; a proposal naming a step the plan does not gate with `proposed` is refused `stage-set`. A work order carries its steps and the union of their reviewers, and a stage is reviewed once, after its last step. The Operations tables and each skill's `references/orchestrated-mode.md` are retired. The five routes and their predicates stay, and `finish` still requires this run's `verify.json` PASS and an independent `qa-gatekeeper` PASS. - Routing: routing entries and `qfai.config.yaml` overrides are keyed by step. A skill that owns steps has no review profile of its own. - The product is unreleased, so no alias, compatibility shim or migration of the old names is added. - Rejected: a `SKILL.md` for each step nested under its skill, because Codex registers nested skills while Claude Code and VS Code do not, so the hosts would disagree on what can be invoked; hidden top-level skills, because each host hides a skill with a different flag; a review at the end of every step, because it multiplies the reviews of a stage. - Amends: DEC-0765, whose sentence that each stage skill declares its operations in an Operations table no longer holds; plans stay built in and are still not an extension point. DEC-0009, as BR-0035 states it, gains the `step/` layer beside `rule/`, `skill/`, `agent/` and `prompt/`. Both rows are left as written. | DONE |

| DEC-0987 | Route requests through a fixed catalog chosen by decision rules, with three upward-only modifiers | - Date: 2026-09-28 - Decided by the user on 2026-09-28, who approved the whole design for implementation. - Evidence: 10,005 requests coded with one codebook — 1,155 from this repository's tracker, 7,650 issues from open-source projects and 1,200 discussions — into 30 intents and 44 work patterns. The ten most frequent patterns cover 61.1% of all items and 85.5% of this repository's; only all 44 cover the open-source tail. On completed items, intent plus entry flags fix the pattern 92.6% of the time once the exits decided by the outcome are set aside, and 35.0% of completed defect reports closed without a change after diagnosis. A second coder recoded 300 items: pattern agreement 76.7% (κ 0.76), 86.1% (κ 0.85) on high-confidence items, intent family 88.0% (κ 0.83), gate 91.3% but κ 0.41; route agreement with the merged catalog 79.7% (κ 0.78), and 72.0% (κ 0.65) on this repository's items. - Decision: (1) Thirty-nine fixed routes in seven families, each running every step of its plan. Adding or dropping steps per request is abolished: the `proposed` predicate, `optionalSteps`, every plan `when`, and the proposal's `candidateRoute` and `requiredStages` go. (2) Three modifiers, `review:heavy`, `gate:user` and `gate:release`: a closed set that only raises review and stops, never changes a step, attaches when any of its signals holds and is never lowered. (3) A closed list of pass-through steps that always run and pass with evidence when they have nothing to write; a pass whose obligation remains is refused. `sdd-story` also passes when a change stays inside the documents that own the truth and adds or changes no example. (4) The agent extracts intent, entry flags, qualifiers, signals, risks, gate, artifacts and confidence; the CLI decides the route with 29 ordered decision rules. (5) Doubt adds a gate: a low-confidence extraction adds `gate:user` and `review:heavy` and asks among the candidate routes; medium confidence adds nothing. (6) Exits without a change are routes, and their nine steps belong to a new parent skill, `qfai-triage`; `qfai-implement` gains 13 steps and `qfai-verify` 6. (7) Deciding and building stay separate routes; a run moves between routes only at declared branch points, at most twice without the operator, and keeps its evidence when the revision is unchanged. (8) `verify-change-note` opens the verify block of every change route. (9) The catalog has no size ceiling; every route added, removed or changed needs a person's approval, recorded as a `Change request:` row and checked in CI. (10) Route ids are verb-object names, and none of the five earlier ids is kept: `direct` becomes `edit-text`, `bugfix` `fix-defect`, `bounded-change` `add-feature`, `feature` `add-feature` or `prototype-feature`, and `discovery` `decide-design`. - Rejected: about 55 fixed routes with each gate and risk variant duplicated as a route, because gates and risks vary independently of the work sequence — one pattern needed the user's decision in only 41% of its items — so every variant doubles routes and thins their evaluation seeds. Composing a plan per request, because the work sequence is fixed at entry 92.6% of the time, no expected plan could be tested, and it restores the per-request step choice this decision abolishes. Seven consistency routes instead of four, because merging them raised route agreement on this repository's items from 68.0% to 72.0% with identical step sequences, and a separate route for aligning to a named owner lowered it to 69.0% (78.3% overall). A ceiling of 50 routes with a second wave held back, because the approval row already bounds growth. The agent choosing a route directly, because an ordered table can be tested exhaustively and its errors traced. One route that decides and then builds, because more than half of the requests to accept an idea never reach building and the two need different interviews. Gating on the extracted gate alone, because its κ is 0.41. - Where: the route catalog, decision rules, modifiers, pass-through checks and branch points in `cli-0015-qfai-workflow.md`; the plan format and the reading of retired route ids in `cli-0020-workflow-files.md`; the new steps in `cli-0002-assistant-steps.md`; `qfai-triage` and the `heavy` review profile in `cli-0001-assistant-routing.md`. The work lands in eleven pull requests: this specification, the engine, the step contents, the catalog, the decision rules, re-routing, extraction, the evaluation seeds and the documentation. | DONE |

The repository root had no `qfai` dependency, so the preflight failed and a bare `npx qfai` fetched the published copy. - Change: the root manifest depends on the package as `"qfai": "workspace:*"`. pnpm links `node_modules/.bin/qfai` to `packages/qfai` once `packages/qfai/dist/` exists, so a maintainer runs `pnpm install`, `pnpm build`, then `pnpm install` again on a fresh clone. No install lifecycle script was added: pnpm links the root's binaries before the root's own `postinstall` or `prepare` runs, so a build there still leaves the link missing until the next install. US-0002-0020 and EX-0002-0020-02 said the root manifest declares no dependency on the package. They now give the reason that still holds: the shipped validate workflow installs without building, so the workspace link has no binary and `npx qfai` there would resolve to the published package.
